runs.notes: file-level green = every executed test in the file passed and the file reported no out-of-test error; all-skipped / no-tests / blocked-external are separate buckets and are NOT passes. The corpus npm dependencies must be installed first (see compat/README.md) -- without them 264 files die at load; test/node_modules is excluded from discovery so third-party packages do not inflate the corpus

direct execution (mbun <file>, exit 0 = pass); node's own harness services (// Flags:, internal bindings) are not emulated, so files needing them count as failures — honest file-level coverage, not API completion. Round-5 derivation: the round-4 full run (pass 1811) plus this round's +24 verified file-level gains (node:path +5, node:url +4, node:vm +6, node:zlib +9), each measured as a zero-regression exit1->exit0 flip against a clean ca818d6 baseline on the full per-subsystem suite. Only those four modules' JS changed, so every other file's classification is unchanged; the 24 gains move fail->pass (1987->1963, 1811->1835). oom-kill/timeout buckets untouched. A fresh full run will be recorded next round.
